item.title: Eric Bauza, the voice acting legend behind Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, and countless other classic characters, has died at 46.
item.description:
Eric Bauza, the voice acting legend behind Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, and countless other classic characters, has died at 46.
Confirmation of Bauza's passing arrived in a post shared on his Instagram account. As reported by KTLA, the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner's Office said he died October 25, 2026, of hypertensive cardiovascular disease.
Additional details surrounding the sudden announcement remain unclear. His family promised to share more soon with a message posted on social media.
"Eric Bauza, Emmy Award-winning voice actor and the modern voice of iconic Looney Tunes characters Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, along with dozens of other beloved cartoon characters, has passed away suddenly," a message from his family said. "More details to come."
Bauza has such a thorough career in animation and voice acting that almost everyone who has enjoyed any TV shows, movies, or games in the last 25 years has probably heard his work. His time lending his unforgettable talent in the industry started with smaller roles in the 2000s, including spots in World of Warcraft, El Tigre: The Adventures of Manny Rivera, Avatar: The Last Airbender, The Sims 2, Chowder, and Alvin and the Chipmunks: The Squeakquel, just to name a few, but it wasn't long before he graduated to become the prolific actor he's known as today.
In the 2010s, Bauza took on parts in video games like Batman: Arkham City, Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance, and Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy 13. Eventually, his work in animation took him to the Looney Tunes universe, where he would go on to play modern iterations on characters like Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Elmer Fudd, Marvin the Martian, and many, many others.
"I’m in complete shock and disbelief," Phineas and Ferb's Vincent Martella said. "A tremendously talented and kind coworker who I always had great conversations with and learned from. Sending so much love to his family. He was a giant. A titan in our industry."
More recently, pop-culture fans may have caught him voicing a few names in Invincible or The Super Mario Galaxy Movie. He also played characters in kids-programming-turned-horror-film Buddy, as well as High on Life 2. Moviegoers heard him reprise his role as Bugs Bunny and other classic Looney Tunes characters in the once-shelved Coyote vs. Acme when it made its way to theaters in August of this year. You can also hear him as Jin-Woo, Kuzon, Pich, and more in Avatar: Seven Havens.
For all intents and purposes, Bauza was a legend not just in animation but entertainment in general. You could fill a book just listing the roles he's played, and that's exactly why the internet has already lit up with friends, fans, and fellow entertainers posting their condolences. IGN interviewed Bauza about how he fought to save Coyote vs. Acme in 2024. You can see some of the ways the internet is remembering the star below.
Still can’t believe it. Eric Bauza was one of the most talented, kind, compassionate, lovable, giving, and wonderful people I’ve ever known. We worked shoulder to shoulder every week during my most formative years. He married my wife and I. We were some of the first people to hold each other’s children. We shared our hopes and dreams and watched each other grow, and I witnessed him become the actor, man, and father he always wanted to be. The world will be a dimmer place for his loss. Love you, buddy.
"I am at a loss for words," Winnie the Pooh actor Jim Cummings shared in a reply to the Instagram post. "Such a young kind man."
"My life was immeasurably changed for the better by having met Eric Bauza," El Tigre creator Jorge R. Gutierrez said. "He just made everything he worked on better. A generational talent. A legend. I would write and design characters giddy thinking how he would bring them to life. And behind the scenes, an incredibly kind, humble and open-hearted good dude. How lucky we all were to have been able to witness his talent shine. And boy did it shine!!! My heart goes out to his family and friends. Adios, amigo. You will never be forgotten."
"I’m so sorry," Ghost of Yōtei star Erika Ishii said. "Much love to you and the rest of the family. He was a good man, a literal voice for change, advocacy, and a pioneer in animation, not to mention the Asian American community. The rest of the voice acting community is here for anything."
I still cant believe this is real. I'm absolutely numb right now. This feels like a bad dream. Eric Bauza was not only one of the most gifted people to grace the voice acting industry and a phenomenally talented artist, but one of the humblest, kindest, most supportive souls in the business. He had the warmest smile and was always sincere. He let his talent speak for itself and made everyone feel like he was their biggest fan. He will always be a legend but I'm devastated that I'll never be able to give him a hug, or hear him joke, or see him smile again. Fuck, man.
Eric Bauza was so kind to me and everyone he interacted with. Such an exuberant and lively soul who never said no when asked to voice these iconic characters. He will be missed. https://t.co/wK0gczaRmT
this fucking sucks, what a loss
Eric Bauza dying might be the worst thing to happen to animation in like decades, im so fr, that man was the modern day Mel blanc. He was SO passionate about carrying on those characters to the modern day, he was such an amazing actor and created so many characters of his own.
Eric Bauza and I didn’t cross paths very often, but you’d never have known it for the genuine warmth and friendliness he showed me every time we did. His talent was only eclipsed by his humility, and that’s saying something. https://t.co/eDkOYMF2C0
We have now lost Peter Cullen and Eric Bauza in the same year. This hurts.💔 https://t.co/uyHrztZc4C
RIP Eric Bauza, the man who brought the Mel Blanc scream back to the Looney Tunes and so much more.
We are deeply saddened to hear of Eric Bauza's passing. His voice talents extended to Ratchet & Clank, Spider-Man, Batman: Arkham City, MultiVersus and so many more. https://t.co/KZwIPnKIin
crazy to think that this is the last time we got to hear him voicing bugs bunny and it almost never got released. he should’ve had way more years ahead of him, still doesn’t make sense that he’s gone. RIP Eric Bauza https://t.co/VZCn8QS8xY

item.title: Bandai Namco has revealed a 10th anniversary update for Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 as fans await the fighting game series' third installment.
item.description:
Bandai Namco has revealed a 10th anniversary update for Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 as fans await the fighting game series' third installment.
The publisher detailed the contents set to drop in the coming days on its website. Split between two major releases – one October 27, the other October 30 – all the new goodies will be available for anyone who has picked up Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 on PC, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One, or Xbox Series X/S since it first launched October 25, 2016.
The first free update is said to bring login bonus rewards, special costumes, and an update for the Future Saga Chapter 4 DLC's Gallery of Time when it launches Tuesday. A true birthday celebration, called "Final Festival of Universes," will follow with hard-to-find items, as well as unlocks for Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3 rewards, come Friday.
"During the Final Festival of Universes, you will be able to raise your camaraderie level with characters who have accompanied you on your journey, choosing between Trunks, The Supreme Kai of Time, or Fu," according to an official description. "Doing so will unlock special illustrations. In addition, hard-to-obtain items will be coming back, and you will be able to earn 25 times more Star Coins than usual, making it easier than ever to exchange them for rewards."
Today marks 10 years since Bandai Namco launched its Dragon Ball action RPG follow-up. The Final Festival of Universes seems to be the publisher's sendoff for the sequel, which makes sense considering there's another game right around the corner.
Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3 was re-revealed for PC and consoles in April of this year and promised to drop players into West City in Age 1000. In an official description shared at the time, Bandai Namco said, "The game combines an epic story-driven RPG experience that will take DRAGON BALL fans on an unforgettable, action-packed journey into this new universe and its cast of characters."
Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3 Screenshots
Fans were hoping the 10-year wait for a third installment wouldn't be too much longer when Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3 was first revealed with its broad 2027 release date. Unfortunately, following narrowed release plans shared earlier this month, it's looking like we'll have to wait another year to go hands-on. When updates will arrive before then is unclear, with producer Masayuki Hirano attributing the slight push back to a desire to "fully realize our ambitions for both the launch experience and the content we plan to operate and support afterward."
The Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 festivities should help the more impatient fans for at least a little while longer. In the meantime, you can read IGN's original 7.5/10 review for the sequel, where we called it "an ambitious, if rough-edged experience, with deceptively deep RPG and brawling elements."

item.title: The #SaveMassEffect movement has picked up even more steam after videos from both Commander Shepard actors – and even posts from the Destiny community – helped its petition reach 200,000 signatures.
item.description:
The #SaveMassEffect movement has picked up even more steam after videos from both Commander Shepard actors – and even posts from the Destiny community – helped its petition reach 200,000 signatures.
It's been a whirlwind week for Mass Effect players and fans of the now-shuttered legendary RPG developer BioWare. After EA announced it would be closing the studio and canceling development for Mass Effect 5, fans took action, and the result is something to behold.
In the first weekend of the #SaveMassEffect movement and its accompanying petition, more than 200,000 verified users have offered their signature to the cause. That's thanks in part to the wild amount of social media attention it's garnered in just a few days, but two of its most prominent supporters have already been backing Mass Effect for decades.
I like this thought…❤️💙#MassEffect #Femshep #broshep #N7 https://t.co/wnCS1I1w0u
"You know what I like to think about?" actor Jennifer Hale, who famously played the female version of Commander Shepard for the first three Mass Effect games, said in a video over the weekend. "I like to think about a world where the fans come together to create a Kickstarter, and then a couple of investors join them, and then a really cool game company joins them. Then a collective is formed to bring Mass Effect back to life for the community, for the creatives – for all of us – and it's amazing. That's what I like to think about."
It's a scenario that fans have pushed for, and one Hale believes in. She had already spoken out about the sadness surrounding BioWare's closure after a leaked trailer for its canceled Mass Effect: Universe project found its way online. At the time, she felt "weirdly hopeful," and just a few days later, she donned the #SaveMassEffect hashtag in a post.
When Hale first shared her feelings about EA's decision to lay off staff and bring the game side of the franchise to a halt, she wasn't alone. Joining her during an Instagram livestream was male Shepard actor Mark Meer. He echoed her thoughts, saying that it was "very sad news" for BioWare's home location in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada, and the industry as a whole. He returned to social media to share a similar video, #SaveMassEffect in tow.
I like it too. Hold the line.#MassEffect #SaveMassEffect #N7 #MassEffectIsAlive #CommanderShepard https://t.co/vx22yejYbR
"I just saw my friend, Jennifer Hale, post about an idea, and I think it's a pretty good one," Meer said. "Save Mass Effect. Hold the line. I should go, and you should go… sign that petition."
At the time of this story's publication, the #SaveMassEffect petition on Change.org, which aims to "prominently illustrate to EA the significance of this iconic series" and demand it continue, has crossed the 200,000-signature mark. It's thanks in part to the continued signal boosting from notable figures like Hale and Meer, who may not have even been included in new Mass Effect games, but they aren't the only ones without a stake in the franchise's future who chose to speak up.
Destiny players, who did their own fair share of organizing when Sony moved to cease development of Destiny 2 content earlier this year, have been a vocal force in the aftermath of BioWare's closure. Although it's hard to say whether organization of this magnitude might impact any decisions to give BioWare developers and their ideas a path forward, the effort is a bit heartwarming to see.
Others from different gaming communities have also done their best to lend a hand. You don't have to search too hard to find posts encouraging anyone who's ever had a brush with Shepard's fight against the Reapers to lend their signature to the cause. Another significant helping hand arrived from developer Owlcat Games, which used the official X/Twitter account for its upcoming game, The Expanse: Osiris Reborn, to ask followers to consider signing the petition in a currently pinned post.
#SaveMassEffect https://t.co/6J8yg2dfCQ
The Expanse show was saved by fans in the past. So the #SaveMassEffect movement has our full support.Please consider signing the petition (link in the quoted post).
Don’t forget, Guardians. We share a bond with Mass Effect. Do your part.#SaveMassEffect https://t.co/EKq0hjssTx
Last month, Destiny players were shocked to hear that Bungie was revisiting its plans for the franchise after its community spoke up. In general, revivals at this level are unlikely, and there's no telling if Mass Effect fans will be quite as lucky, but for now, fans don't seem to show any sign of stopping. While we wait to see what is, hopefully, next for the legendary sci-fi RPG series, you can learn more about Mass Effect: Universe thanks to some recently leaked gameplay details. You can also read about the fans hoping to organize a boycott against EA.

item.title: Professor X actor Christopher Abbott said Marvel fans won't see him in Avengers: Doomsday or Secret Wars because he needs to wrap up his time with X-Men before doing any cameos.
item.description:
Professor X actor Christopher Abbott said Marvel fans won't see him in Avengers: Doomsday or Secret Wars because he needs to wrap up his time with X-Men before doing any cameos.
The Marvel Cinematic Universe newcomer tried his best not to play coy during a conversation with Rolling Stone. When pressed on whether comic book fans will see his shaved head fighting against Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom at any point in the next year or so, he insisted he doesn't have any additional team-up movies on his plate for now.
"I don't think so," when asked if he'll appear in any cameo roles before X-Men. "I don't even know… See, what's happening? What do you mean?"
Christopher Abbott, who will play Professor X in 2028's ‘X-Men’ reboot, says he will not be in the upcoming Avengers movie.“I don't think so. Well, I don't even know–what's happening? What do you mean? I don't know what's going on. On no. I'm not in that. I gotta do the ‘X-Men’ movie first before any of that stuff.”
When the interviewer clarified, asking if he'll play in Doomsday, he had a quick reply: "No, I'm not in that."
Abbott joined a cast of other would-be mutant heroes when Marvel Studios confirmed he had been picked to play Professor X at D23 earlier this year. The announcement also came with a May 2028 release date, giving him plenty of time to prepare to play the group's leader, and if fans are lucky, show up for a scene or two beforehand.
After all, Doomsday and Secret Wars aren't just your run-of-the-mill superhero flicks. These are saga-ending event films packed to the gills with A-listers and, of course, cameos to keep the MCU going well into the future. With the 2000s versions of the X-Men, including Patrick Stewart's version of Charles Xavier, having already shown up for a few Doomsday trailers, many have wondered if the new X-Men cast would show up on-screen before Marvel's 2027 slate launched. If Abbott is out, though, the chances of an early MCU debut for other X-Men (besides Sadie Sink's Jean Grey) just got a little less likely.
"I gotta do the X-Men movie first before any of that stuff," he continued.
MCU X-Men Cast as of D23 2026
When the interviewer interjected, pointing out that hard launching characters without a cameo is "famously not how Marvel works," Abbott said with a chuckle, "Look, no coyness: I'm not in that movie."
With Doomsday less than two months from its December 18, 2026, release date, it really does sound like Abbott won't show up. However, his answer regarding Secret Wars, the only other movie between now and X-Men, didn't seem quite as definitive. With more than a full year before that film follows come December 17, 2027, and no trailers out yet, who knows? That said, at least as far as this new take on Professor X is concerned, it is still probably best not to get hopes up too high in the meantime.
Set to join Abbott on the team are Inde Navarrette as Rogue, Maya Boyd as Storm, Asa Germann as Angel, and more. We'll at least see the X-Men team unite when the reboot premieres May 5, 2028. Until then, you can get a sneak peek at Navarrette's progress on developing Rogue's accent.
Photo by ANGELA WEISS / AFP via Getty Images.

item.title: Clayface looks set up to be a win for the DCU after securing the top spot at the box office with an estimated global haul of $43 million.
item.description:
Clayface looks set up to be a win for the DCU after securing the top spot at the box office with an estimated global haul of $43 million.
It's a strong start for the low-budget DCU film, split between $24 million domestically and $19 million internationally. The opening weekend total falls toward the higher end of early projections as audiences showed up to see Tom Rhys Harries bring a twisted and often overlooked Batman villain to the big screen.
With brutal body horror elements in a story that sees the birth of its titular character, Clayface follows Matt Hagen as he attempts to rebuild his life after a horrible attack leaves his face scarred. Starring Harries, directed by James Watkins, and written by Mike Flanagan and Hossein Amini, this latest DCU movie took viewers into the darkest corners of James Gunn and Peter Safran's universe they've seen yet, with a pretty hard-R rating.
It's for these reasons that the DCU's foray into a new live-action Gotham City left fans with question marks as they feared how a more adult-oriented story could fit into the same world as something as bubbly and bright as 2025's Superman. So far, at least, it seems to have paid off, at least compared to Supergirl, which landed as a dud in the DCU earlier this year.
The Milly Alcock-led superhero movie was deemed a box office bomb after it premiered in June. That's mostly due to its almost $200 million budget, which towered over the comparatively measly $126.46 million it gathered throughout its run (via Box Office Mojo). Clayface, on the other hand, is starting its time in theaters almost matching the $44 million budget reported by Variety.
Although there is certainly plenty of ground to cover before officially being declared a success, it seems like a strong start. A few factors will help carry Clayface throughout the rest of its run: Firstly, its October release timing means Halloween moviegoers will have something spooky to watch next weekend. Reviews have been pretty solid, too, with Rotten Tomatoes recording a 75% from critics and 94% from audiences.

item.title: Additional details about BioWare's canceled Mass Effect game have leaked online, revealing a story that would have taken choices from the Commander Shepard trilogy into account if EA hadn't shut down the studio.
item.description:
Additional details about BioWare's canceled Mass Effect game have leaked online, revealing a story that would have taken choices from the Commander Shepard trilogy into account if EA hadn't shut down the studio.
The long-awaited and currently canned follow-up for the sci-fi RPG franchise, which was working under the title Mass Effect: Universe, was built around decisions made in the original games, according to comments shared by former technical director Romain Toutain during a recent livestream (via Kotaku). As more details about the project leak, there's no telling exactly how thorough this system would have been, but he did his best to give fans an idea.
"All the choices made in the first Mass Effect games were taken into account," Toutain said (translation via Bluesky user @loustica-lucia.bsky.social). "One of the reasons why it was called 'Mass Effect: Universe' is that you had so many choices. That you could plug your saves together to create parallel universes, to keep it simple. It's not exactly how it worked. You had different timelines, basically."
Every IGN Mass Effect Review
Mass Effect fans know how crucial the series' overarching story is, especially when it comes to Commander Shepard's first three installments in his/her fight against the Reapers. Outside of the ill-fated Andromeda follow-up that launched in 2017, players were able to carry major choices from each entry over to the next, resulting in a trilogy of games with a highly personalized story.
Relationships, major character deaths, and even the fate of an entire species are just a few of the ways Shepard can be steered to shape the galaxy, and although whether it was all worth it in the end is still up for debate, it seems Mass Effect: Universe would have offered an opportunity to right some wrongs. Toutain said they had plans for those who just prefer to experiment with the story and its many, many branches, too. He likened the freedom to "generate timelines" to Spike Chunsoft's 2016 video game, Zero Time Dilemma.
"You have no f**king idea just how great it was," he continued. Then, responding to a fan asking whether Mass Effect: Universe would have featured systems similar to what was found in Dragon Age: Inquisition and the series' lore-tailoring Keep application, he said, "kinda, yeah."

item.title: Manni L. Perez, the actress long rumored to be playing Lucia in GTA 6, has gone viral after dodging a swarm of comments from Grand Theft Auto fans during a recent livestream.
item.description:
Manni L. Perez, the actress long rumored to be playing Lucia in GTA 6, has gone viral after dodging a swarm of comments from Grand Theft Auto fans during a recent livestream.
Rockstar Games has refrained from confirming the vast majority of the cast of next month's new GTA game, but as if there was ever any doubt, that hasn't stopped ravenous fans from piecing a list together themselves. Perez is one name theorists have talked about for years, so she took a few minutes to let thousands of viewers get to know her while masterfully dodging a swarm of GTA 6 comments along the way.
Reaching a peak of more than 2,100 viewers on a six-month-old Instagram account with just nine posts, Perez spent her 12-minute livestream just talking about her life growing up in a "small, rural, redneck-y" town. She lives in a studio apartment with a dog, loves to cook, grew up driving trucks, and as far as everyone else is officially concerned, she definitely will not be the star of the so-called biggest video game of all time in a little less than a month.
"But yeah, no, I'm not rich. I'm a regular person," Perez said when responding to fans who assumed she was wealthy. "I live in a small studio apartment, which I love. I have my tiny, little itty-bitty kitchen, and it's just me and my dog. I do everything on my own, and I've done everything on my own for a very long time, and I love it, and I'm very grateful. I have a family that loves me, and I'm just feeling like I'm in a really good place, where I am in my life."
"I want a green truck," she said with a smile while ignoring the horde comments mentioning "Lucia" and "GTA 6." Some responded that, no, actually, she doesn't live alone, because she has Jason to keep her company. Others were subtler, asking if she'll be playing Rockstar's latest or if she's just "ready for next month." Despite the steady flow of responses begging her to confirm her alleged role – which would be guarded under a strict non-disclosure agreement, even if it were real – Perez only acknowledged users commenting about anything else.
Keep in mind that this all comes from years of clues gathered by fans, but Rockstar's lack of confirmation doesn't mean there's nothing to suggest Perez is playing Lucia in GTA 6. As others have highlighted, the actress has a history of live-action and voice roles. She has credits for single episodes of shows like Jessica Jones, The Blacklist, and Law & Order: Special Victims Unit. Funnily enough, she also played a blackjack dealer in Grand Theft Auto Online.
Her place in Rockstar history may be given a bump when GTA 6 launches for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S next month, November 19. If you're wondering who might be playing Lucia's partner in crime, Jason, fans have long speculated that Modern Family and Grey's Anatomy actor Dylan Rourke filled the role, but he, too, has yet to be confirmed.
Who has been confirmed, whether Rockstar and any likely NDAs like it or not, is Stephen Root, who said he will be seen playing drug trafficker Brian Heder. Otherwise, we might need to wait until launch to see the full cast, so don't go sending messages to any actors just yet.
Fans may have tracked down the voice actors behind one of the biggest game launches of all time, but it's par for the course when it comes to Grand Theft Auto players. One fan spent three months charting planetary positions just to try and learn when trailer 3 would premiere (they were wrong). Another fan measured oxygen levels to try and achieve the same feat (they, too, were wrong).

item.title: A knife-wielding man was arrested Friday night for threatening crew members on the Brooklyn set of Miami Vice ‘85. Citing information from the NYPD, TMZ reports that a police officer working security on the set arrested Alex Perez, 23.
item.description:
A knife-wielding man was arrested Friday night for threatening crew members on the Brooklyn set of Miami Vice ‘85.
Citing information from the NYPD, TMZ reports that a police officer working security on the set arrested Alex Perez, 23, who has a criminal record.
“Perez can be seen being escorted off the set by a staffer before taking out the large knife from his sweatshirt pocket,” according to TMZ, which also posted a video of the incident.
“A cop on the scene then arrested Perez -- who hurled the n-word at the production staff member while in cuffs -- at 11:17 PM.”
The site reports that Perez has been charged with menacing with a weapon in the 2nd degree and criminal possession of a weapon in the 4th degree.
Miami Vice ‘85 has been filming in New York this week, including scenes featuring Michael B. Jordan and John Leguizamo in that appear to faithfully recreate the opening moments of the original TV series’ pilot.
Director Joseph Kosinski’s film is inspired by the series’ two-part pilot (“Brother’s Keeper”) and the show’s first season in general.
For more on Miami Vice ‘85, check out these first look images of Jordan and Austin Butler in costume as detectives Ricardo Tubbs and Sonny Crockett, respectively.
Miami Vice ‘85 will relocate production to Miami, Florida after hurricane season is over. The film opens in theaters on May 19, 2028.

item.title: Marvel dropped a new trailer for Avengers: Doomsday that leans heavily on the dynamic between Thor and Steve Rogers, especially their shared worthiness to wield the enchanted hammer Mjolnir.
item.description:
Marvel dropped a new trailer for Avengers: Doomsday on Saturday, roughly 24 hours after debuting a Major League Baseball crossover promo during the World Series.
This new trailer – which can be seen below – leans heavily on the dynamic between Thor (Chris Hemsworth) and Steve Rogers (Chris Evans), their shared worthiness to wield the enchanted hammer Mjolnir.
Thor appears to be the leader of the Avengers here, at one point rallying the troops to take on Doctor Doom, saying, “Doom will tear this world apart. Team up and stand together.”
Paul Rudd’s Ant-Man once again brings levity to the proceedings in a scene that pokes fun at the multiple men present who have carried the mantle of Captain America (Steve, Sam Wilson, and USAgent, who points out, “I was also Cap for a minute.”).
The new promo comes on the heels of the news that Project Hail Mary’s Sandra Hüller has been cast in Doomsday in an undisclosed role and David Harbour’s insistence that he didn’t spoil the flm in a recent interview.
Meanwhile, Marvel fans think they’ve figured out which character was edited out of the first Doomsday trailer.
Marvel’s Avengers: Doomsday opens in theaters on December 18.

item.title: DC Studios co-chairman James Gunn has defended the DCU's approach to interconnected stories, saying he doesn't want movies like Clayface to exist just to "set up" crossovers.
item.description:
DC Studios co-chairman James Gunn has defended the DCU's approach to interconnected stories, saying he doesn't want movies like Clayface to exist just to "set up" crossovers.
Clayface poured into the DCU when it brought the tragic story of Matt Hagen (Tom Rhys Harries) to theaters yesterday. A bloody body horror movie with a firm R rating, its October release date makes sense as it molded its way into the comic book movie universe with a more adult story, but not everyone is happy with the film's place in the universe.
Despite solid scores from critics and fans (IGN gave it a 7/10 review), there are DC watchers who have continued to complain that executives like Gunn and co-chairman Peter Safran haven't done a good job of using smaller stories to build toward bigger tie-in projects. For reference, the DCU technically started with animated series Creature Commandos before heading to theaters with Superman. Peacemaker Season 2, Supergirl, Lanterns, and Clayface then followed.
While standalone Wonder Woman and Batman movies are in the cards, projects like The People v. Gorilla Grodd seem to be further along than most, with crossover moments mostly limited so far. So, what gives? Gunn has an easy answer that might leave impatient fans wanting more, but for him, it's a solution that will keep the DCU telling quality stories for years to come.
"I couldn't agree more," he said when replying to a fan defending the cinematic universe on Threads. "DCU is just an alternate universe; we can enter at any location or time and tell THAT story. I dislike the idea that individual stories aren't meaningful unless they lead to something else."
Gunn continued, saying it's "strange" to see "people not understanding this" considering Star Wars has taken a similar approach for decades. He did admit Disney's sci-fi franchise may not have the "tonal variety" of something like the DCU, which has so far ping-ponged between serious drama and action to comedy and, most recently, horror. Still, he wants fans to know that, no matter how different each movie or show may be, there is still connective tissue holding them together.

item.title: Call of Duty movie director Peter Berg has teased more details from his live-action film, promising an adaptation with "a very strong soul" that explores "the cost of war."
item.description:
Call of Duty movie director Peter Berg has teased more details from his live-action film, promising an adaptation with "a very strong soul" that explores "the cost of war."
The filmmaker behind Skydance-Paramount's upcoming reimagining of Activision's massive first-person shooter series dived into his thoughts on the franchise during an interview with ComicBook. We already know the Call of Duty movie will focus on the Modern Warfare portion of the FPS universe, and it sounds like Berg and writer Taylor Sheridan have already looked to the games it's based on for inspiration.
"So Modern Warfare, if you really look at the missions, and the storylines, and the characters – like Captain Price, and Soap, and Ghost, and Alex – these are complicated humans," Berg said. "These are not – and no disrespect – cartoon characters or comic books. These are very nuanced storylines; like, there's a real soul to the Modern Warfare universe…
The Best Video Game Movies of All Time
"And, yes, there's violence, and there's hardware, and equipment, and there's killing – but underneath it I think the game, and the craters of the game, are really looking at the cost of war, the cost of having to be a warrior who's, for whatever reason, chosen to put himself between real danger and the rest of us, and the burden that these guys carry."
Berg seems to be putting in the work to nail a Modern Warfare story for the big screen, but not every fan is convinced that he's the right guy for the job. That's mostly because he had some not-so-nice things to say about gaming back in 2013. When asked for his take on video games based on war at the time, he said, called them "pathetic," using the term, "keyboard courage."
"I think anyone that sits around playing video games for four hours... It's weak," Berg elaborated at the time. "Get out, do something."
These days he's changed his tune, and judging by his affection for characters like Captain Price and Ghost, he's hoping to do right by Modern Warfare and its fans. His upcoming film, The Mosquito Bowl, is a sports-war film set to premiere later this month. His vision for the Call of Duty movie will start to take shape after that.
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Campaign Screenshots
"And that’s real stuff," Berg added when talking about Modern Warfare's connection to the real-life cost of war. "This is not just 'Hey, let’s shoot them all up and shoot popcorn!' Like, there’s a soul underneath it, that I understand that Taylor Sheridan understands, and I think probably not quite as graphically violent as Mosquito Bowl, but there will be a very strong soul, and consequence of war within the film, called 'duty.'"
The Modern Warfare universe most recently expanded with the release of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, which concluded Activision and Infinity Ward's reboot story when it launched yesterday. Its story has been called one of the darker entries the franchise has offered in recent memory.

item.title: Alex Garland's Elden Ring movie reportedly carries a hefty budget of almost $200 million, making it A24's most expensive movie ever – and it's not close.
item.description:
Alex Garland's Elden Ring movie reportedly carries a hefty budget of almost $200 million, making it A24's most expensive movie ever – and it's not close.
Background information on the live-action adaptation of FromSoftware and George R.R. Martin's 2022 RPG was shared in a Wall Street Journal report. The site stated that, according to its sources, Elden Ring's budget is "nearly $200 million."
That makes it far and away the most expensive movie for the arthouse film-focused company, which has built a reputation for delivering memorable projects on more modest budgets for the last 14 years. Should Elden Ring's reported budget prove accurate, it would mean Garland's film falls in line with Marvel movies like Spider-Man: No Way Home ($200 million via Variety) and Jurassic World Rebirth ($180 million via The Hollywood Reporter).
The 24 Best A24 Movies
As seen in 2025's Marty Supreme, that's a far cry from A24's usual strategy. The Timothée Chalamet-led, Josh Safdie-directed drama made headlines ahead of its release for being the most expensive film the company had produced at $70 million (via Deadline).
That puts Elden Ring at nearly three times the cost of A24's next-most-expensive picture. Garland's Civil War supposedly cost $50 million before that, according to Variety. Dwayne 'The Rock' Johnson's The Smashing Machine reportedly carried a similar budget. In other words, nothing really comes close to A24's first major swing in the world of video game movie adaptations.
For now, we know little about Elden Ring ahead of its 2028 premiere, so it's hard to say exactly why it costs so much. Earlier this year, the movie studio announced the film had a pretty stacked cast, which includes familiar faces like Kit Connor (X-Men, Warfare), Cailee Spaeny (Alien: Romulus, Civil War), Nick Offerman (The Last of Us, Parks and Recreation), Havana Rose Liu (Tuner, Bottoms), and more. Early production photos then teased faithful recreations of some iconic sets, with more making their way to the internet not long after.
Elden Ring Movie Cast
The Elden Ring movie's big budget may not have always been the plan for what's shaping up to, one way or another, be a massive release for A24. Previous reports had the live-action fantasy flick pinned at just more than $100 million, suggesting either that initial rumors were inaccurate or Garland's budget somehow ballooned over the course of production. Filming finally wrapped in July of this year.
The Elden Ring movie was announced in May 2025 and is expected to premiere March 3, 2028. It will probably be a little while longer before we see any official images or a trailer, so in the meantime, you can read about how actor and Dark Souls superfan Peter Serafinowicz landed a role in the film.

item.title: Marvel fans say the new Avengers: Doomsday teaser might have revealed who was edited out of its first trailer.
item.description:
Marvel fans say the new Avengers: Doomsday teaser might have revealed who was edited out of its first trailer.
Marvel Studios didn't not reveal more from its December team-up movie when the Doomsday baseball teaser premiered during Game 1 of the 2026 World Series last night. Focusing more on letting Pedro Pascal's Reed Richards throw Joseph Quinn's Johnny Storm a stretchy pitch as MLB players did their best to fit in, the minute-long TV spot felt more like a cute crossover than an opportunity for new footage – but that doesn't mean fans aren't still all over it.
In between the shots of the Fantastic Four's Earth-828 are, occasionally, what amounts to a few precious seconds of new footage from Avengers: Doomsday. With less than two months left to go until the premiere, Marvel really only took the time to highlight some funny interactions between Steve Rogers (Chris Evans) and characters like Ant-Man (Paul Rudd) and Thor (Chris Hemsworth).
Worlds collide ⚾An exclusive preview of Marvel's new Avengers movie assembles Bryce Harper, Freddie Freeman, Jacob Misiorowski, Junior Caminero and Randy Arozarena 👀Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters everywhere December 18 https://t.co/WX1YtKjAKt
It's…not much. While you might think Steve taking a jab at Thor while wielding Mjolnir is the standout moment, some eagle-eyed fans think it's the scene the former Captain America shares with Ant-Man that we should be paying attention to.
Let's take a step back. You might remember Marvel fans doing what they do best by looking for clues tucked into the original Doomsday trailer. One shot that caught a lot of attention was an image showing the New Avengers having a meeting with old heroes and the Fantastic Four. A gap between the Earth-828 heroes led many to believe Marvel had, as it's been known to do before, edited out an important character from the scene.
The World Series teaser took viewers back and showed that scene from a new perspective, bringing Steve Rogers along as a plus one. The quick shot of Evans' character showed that he's almost certainly standing next to Ebon Moss-Bachrach's Ben Grimm as he does his best to entertain Scott Lang. With Evans unseen in the previously questionable look at the scene, Marvel fans believe Steve Rogers was the character Marvel was trying to hide all along.
Steve being next to Ben confirms he was edited out of the first trailer. He is next to Ben, Sam and Scott https://t.co/FS8To3Z7nt
"Yup, and Doom is edited out too," another fan said, referencing a theory that Doctor Doom may appear as an ally during the events of the film. "I wonder if they will show it in the trailers, hopefully they do just a tiny bit."
And ta-da: We finally seem to have our answer – but why? Why would Marvel edit out a character that fans are already well aware had a role to play in Doomsday? It's confusing, especially considering Steve does eventually show up later in the trailer he's believed to have been edited out of.
On the other side of things are those still trying to determine if the person we've seen wielding Mjolnir is even Steve Rogers at all. One popular fan theory that has gained more traction as Evans' role is once again put under the microscope is that his character is actually Tom Hiddleston's Loki in disguise. Some also suspect that the original trailer wasn't ever edited in the first place, with this new footage simply showing the same scene but a few seconds before or after that shot of questionable positioning.
Was Marvel playing with its hero positioning just to give its first trailer a bit more punch toward the end, is there more mystery to solve, or are fans maybe looking too much into things? That's the main conversation fans are having in the aftermath of just a few frames of new Doomsday footage.
Holdup https://t.co/A3arrek86n
this sounds exactly like something Loki would say to Thor as steve rogers 😭 https://t.co/OUEmvJubQu
"In the new trailer, I can't be the only one, Steve's face or something looks weird like it kept changing in each scene or something else," one theorist said. "I can't quite put my finger on it but something about him is off."
As ridiculous as some of this might sound, Marvel has absolutely played with pre-release footage to throw fans off the scent of big reveals before. Marketing materials released in the lead-up to Avengers: Infinity War in 2018 provide a few of the most notable examples, with many seemingly important scenes featured in trailers completely cut from the final version of the film. Searching for potential edits with a fine-tooth comb is also something Marvel fans did ahead of the release of Spider-Man: Brand New Day.
Should Steve Rogers be a major focus in Avengers: Doomsday?

item.title: Marvel Studios debuted a unique promo for Avengers: Doomsday during Game 1 of the 2026 World Series on Fox tonight between the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays. The ad is an Avengers-MLB crossover set on Earth-828 at Ebbets Field (the former home of the Dodgers when they were in Brooklyn; it was torn down on our Earth in 1960 – the promo is seemingly set in the same time period as The Fantastic Four: First Steps, as you can see New York Giants players in the background).
item.description:
Marvel Studios debuted a unique promo for Avengers: Doomsday during Game 1 of the 2026 World Series on Fox tonight between the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays. The ad is an Avengers-MLB crossover set on Earth-828 at Ebbets Field (the former home of the Dodgers when they were in Brooklyn; it was torn down on our Earth in 1960 – the promo is seemingly set in the same time period as The Fantastic Four: First Steps, as you can see New York Giants players in the background).
In it, Mr. Fantastic, sporting a Brooklyn Dodgers cap, takes the mound to throw a stretchy-armed first pitch while The Thing hypes up the players as current, modern MLB players Freddie Freeman, Jacob Misiorowski, Bryce Harper, Randy Arozarena, and Junior Caminero look on from the sidelines. They're interrupted when Dr. Doom attacks from the sky, with clips from the film interspersed throughout the promo.
Worlds collide ⚾An exclusive preview of Marvel's new Avengers movie assembles Bryce Harper, Freddie Freeman, Jacob Misiorowski, Junior Caminero and Randy Arozarena 👀Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters everywhere December 18 https://t.co/WX1YtKjAKt
Live sporting events, such as the Super Bowl, NBA Finals, and World Series remain one of Hollywood's favorite mediums to debut new trailers and promote films, as in the age of streaming and on-demand content, they're one of the few forms of programming that consistently drive a live, tuned-in audience.
Avengers: Doomsday returns Chris Evans as Steve Rogers (which is referenced in a clip from the film used in the MLB promo), while Robert Downey Jr. trades Iron Man's mask for Dr. Doom's and appears to be abducting heroes in the upcoming film (though we will see RDJ as Stark at least one more time, starting in 2028 at Disney California Adventure's upcoming Avengers: Infinity Defense ride). Much of it remains shrouded in mystery, such that even actors in the film don't know what happens.
Audience interest appears to be strong, as ticket pre-sales are outpacing those of this summer's blockbuster hit Spider-Man: Brand New Day. But Marvel recommends you do your homework before heading to the theater for Doomsday.

item.title: Dead by Daylight fans are beside themselves after Behaviour Interactive announced that all Chucky content would no longer be available to purchase starting next month.
item.description:
Dead by Daylight fans are beside themselves after Behaviour Interactive announced that all Chucky content would no longer be available to purchase starting next month.
The developer behind the popular asymmetrical horror game confirmed plans to pull the Chucky Chapter from sale in posts shared across social media. The message followed rumors that the possessed killer doll would soon be removed from the game, with the official statement promising that those who have purchased related content will be able to use it even after it is removed from shelves starting November 24, 2026.
"We welcomed The Good Guy out of his box and into The Fog nearly three years ago, but it's now time for the Chucky Chapter to leave the shelf," Behaviour said. "On November 24, 2026, the Chapter and its associated content will be removed from in-game and first-party stores. Any content unlocked before that date will remain available to use in-game."
Dead by Daylight x Chucky Screenshots
As detailed in an FAQ post shared by the developers, these changes to the Chucky Chapter mean a few things for Dead by Daylight players. Its Killer, known in-game as The Good Guy, will no longer be available to purchase, though bug fixes will still be supported. The collection of outfits and cosmetics he's gained since being added in 2023 will also be made unavailable, and no future add-ons for the character will be added.
In other words, if you're a Chucky fan who's been waiting to pull the trigger, you might want to start thinking about it. To help ease players into the idea of losing one of Dead by Daylight's most unique Killers, Behaviour is holding a sale for all items related to the Chucky Chapter starting Monday, October 26. The "Last Chance" sale runs until his November 24 removal date and slashes prices by 50% across all platforms.
Dead by Daylight and its collection of Killers has often been referred to as 'horror Super Smash Bros.' by fans, but Behaviour has plenty of experience when it comes to pulling Killers. Hellraiser's Pinhead was pulled from digital storefronts in 2025 after first joining in 2021. Halloween's Michael Myers, the first major playable Killer to join Dead by Daylight after its launch in 2016, was removed this past January.
@DeadbyDaylight I THOUGHT WE HAD A NICE LICENSE AGREEMENT!!!!! https://t.co/bOMgT44DQt
Although Behaviour refrained from sharing more details about why exactly the Child's Play rep is being removed, fans usually assume licensing issues are to blame. Hellraiser and Halloween both received new game announcements in Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival and Halloween: The Game that just happened to arrive around the time their respective properties were pulled from Dead by Daylight. Friday the 13th's infamous licensing kerfuffle is also allegedly what kept Jason Voorhees out of The Fog for years before he finally joined a few months back. Stranger Things is another example, with its first chapter's Demogorgon content removed before returning in 2023.
Like Chucky, players who purchased pulled content can still use it freely even after it's removed from stores, but that doesn't mean other players can't feel the impact. Content being removed from purchase not only means that players won't be able to buy it in the future; it means that content will likely show up less frequently during matches.
That affects just about everyone who likes having their Survivor matches shaken up by new Killer abilities to keep them on their toes, as a player doesn't need to have purchased a chapter to play against its respective Killer. Considering Michael Myers left Dead by Daylight earlier this year and Pinhead was removed not much longer before that, players are feeling Chucky's pull from sale more than many of the previous Killer removals.
"Hold a license challenge: impossible," one fan said.
"How do you keep losing licenses bro?" another fan speculated. "I thought you had a good relationship. Chucky had many skins WTF :("
goodbye chuckster. i will always love you https://t.co/h6sUaDGrwI
Again, Behaviour has not explicitly stated why new players will not be able to purchase Chucky after that November cutoff date. IGN has reached out to the Dead by Daylight team for comment.
"This makes me so sad," one player on Reddit said. "Chucky is such a huge license and we've lost Michael and Pinhead already within the last two years. Not blaming BHVR for it, I get it's business. It just sucks."
"It's strange though. You'd assume they'd change their contractual agreements after losing Demogorgon the first time to prevent this from happening with recent Killers," another replied. "Michael/Pinhead are a bit understandable since those were older licenses, but I'd assume Chucky would've had a proactive contractual agreement to prevent this from happening?"
Dead by Daylight 10th Anniversary Broadcast Visual Overhaul Reveal - Screenshots
Although losing three Killers in the span of a year and a half might sting, Behaviour has continued to add new notable characters and franchises into the mix. After Tokyo Ghoul's Ken Kaneki and Five Nights at Freddy's Springtrap were added last year, the studio brought Stranger Things villain Vecna into The Fog. Jason joined in the summer of this year, and Terrifier's Art the Clown will be added next month. Although the majority of the game's licensed Killers have remained available for years and are still available to this day, how long they will remain available for purchase is unclear.
Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

item.title: Marvel has reportedly cast Sandra Hüller in Avengers: Doomsday for a secret cameo role.
item.description:
Marvel has reportedly cast Sandra Hüller in Avengers: Doomsday for a secret cameo role.
Information about the last-minute addition comes from The Hollywood Reporter, which said the Project Hail Mary star will appear on screens when Earth's Mightiest Heroes take on Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom this December. Although much of that cast and their parts in the movie have been confirmed, details about Hüller's role were not shared.
Marvel Studios and directors Joe and Anthony Russo almost certainly have plans for plenty of superhero moments and surprises. How Hüller fits into that plan remains to be seen, but considering fans had already speculated about her involvement in recent days, some of the less patient Marvel Cinematic Universe enjoyers are probably already doing their best to piece together Doomsday's mysteries early.
Hüller is a German actor with a decades-long career on movie and TV screens. She was nominated for Actress in a Leading Role at the 2024 Oscars for her part in Anatomy of a Fall, but is also known for her parts in films like Digger, The Zone of Interest, and Fatherland. If you missed her in any of those movies, there's a good chance you caught her playing Eva Stratt, a role that we called one of the best parts of Ryan Gosling's Project Hail Mary.
As for her Marvel introduction, all we know for now is that she'll appear in a cameo part, meaning she probably won't show up for much of its 2-hour-and-45-minute runtime. Like major stars – including Harry Styles and Charlize Theron – before her, it's possible that we could only see Hüller's character during a stinger moment shown during the film's credits sequence. There's at least little reason to suspect that's not on the table, especially considering Marvel will use Doomsday's plot to set up the release of Avengers: Secret Wars in December 2027.
Doomsday is out in just a few short months, but that clearly hasn't stopped Marvel from revealing new information for what's gearing up to be one of the year's biggest releases. Even more about the movie is expected to be revealed at the MLB World Series, which is just a few hours after this piece's publication. THR noted that the Russo brothers are knee-deep in post-production for the film ahead of its December 18, 2026, premiere.

Avengers: Doomsday will bring the Avengers, X-Men, Fantastic Four, and more when it arrives in a few months. Until then, you can read what Jeremy Renner had to say about the good guys' chances without Hawkeye. You can also see how David Harbour did his best to walk back what may have been an early spoiler.

item.title: Helen Chiang, Xbox’s first-ever chief operating officer, is no longer in the role just three months after it was created, as told by CEO Asha Sharma in an internal memo today.
item.description:
Helen Chiang, Xbox’s first-ever chief operating officer, is no longer in the role just three months after it was created, as told by CEO Asha Sharma in an internal memo today.
The memo, verified by The Verge, included a brief statement from Sharma regarding Chiang’s exit. “Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft today. I’m grateful for her years of service and wish her well,” Sharma said. “We’ll share more on COO leadership as plans are finalized.”
Chiang had been with Xbox for an astonishing 21 years. Previously, she was in charge of the Minecraft franchise, and shifted roles to chief operating officer in July 2026.
Xbox and IKEA Furniture Collaboration Photos
The reason for Chiang’s promotion and the job duties of the COO were outlined in a statement by Sharma amid news of Xbox’s massive restructuring this summer. According to Sharma, the role was necessary to “work toward a shared goal, make the right tradeoffs, and get things done” as Xbox’s headcount grew and the company became “more fragmented.”
“For the first time, we are establishing a Chief Operating Officer with end-to-end P&L responsibility across content, hardware, platform, and services. Helen Chiang has been promoted to this role and will report directly to me,” Sharma said at the time.
“Over nearly two decades at Xbox, Helen has helped build some of our most important businesses, from Xbox Live to leading Mojang and the Minecraft franchise. She will bring our businesses together under one operating model, making sure we make clear investment decisions, learn from our successes and failures, and hold ourselves accountable for results.”
As noted by The Verge, the reason for Chiang’s brief tenure in this specific role has not yet been divulged, but it’s certainly a striking move, given her 21 years with the company prior to this.
Xbox is predicted to continue layoffs as part of its ongoing internal restructuring, with 3,200 total employees expected to lose their jobs this year. Several studios have been divested as a result of this rework, though some have managed to find their footing, as is the case with Double Fine.
Others, however, remain in limbo; Arkane Lyon, the studio that’s currently working on Marvel’s Blade, faces closure as soon as mid-November if a buyer isn’t found. The studio was also impacted by the reshuffling at Microsoft, leaving both fans and industry insiders biting their nails in hope that the project finds a new home.
Marvel's Blade Concept Art
Other companies in the games industry aren’t faring any better. Just this week, EA announced the closure of 30-year-old RPG powerhouse BioWare, known for making games like Dragon Age, Jade Empire, and Mass Effect. The next Mass Effect game was also canceled, prompting worldwide outcry from players and calls for a boycott.
A full-length trailer for the game was also leaked online, rubbing more salt in the wound thanks to just how fantastic it looked. And while fans are crossing their fingers that EA either sells BioWare’s IP or hands them over to another studio, analysts say this isn’t likely. Oh, well — at least the Prime Video series is still alive.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: The developer of a zombie game set in San Francisco has removed the game from online marketplaces and issued a public apology after city officials condemned the title for depicting its homeless people as ‘zombies.’
item.description:
The developer of a zombie game set in San Francisco has taken down the game and issued a public apology after city officials condemned the title for depicting its citizens as ‘zombies.’
Tenderloin Night Shift was a vibe-coded, first-person shooter created by independent developer Pierre-Louis Biojout over the course of a weekend using OpenAI’s Codex. As you’ve probably inferred by its title, the game takes place in San Francisco’s Tenderloin neighborhood, an area infamous for its high crime rates and unhoused population that’s often compared offhandedly to Los Angeles’s Skid Row.
In the game, players use a gun to rid the Tenderloin of ‘zombies.’ Some of these undead enemies wear construction uniforms or whiz by on motorized scooters, while others wear food delivery backpacks, having clearly been infected while on the job. Still others are depicted doing the ‘fentanyl fold,’ a position where the body is bent forward at the waist, most usually displayed by fentanyl users who seem to have been frozen while standing upright.
The Best Zombie Movies
“San Francisco couldn’t fix the tenderloin, so I monetized it,” Biojout said on social media. In the game, he sold digital ad space for $100 per week, which accounts for some of the real-world companies seen on billboards within his polygonal recreation of the neighborhood.
It didn’t take long for San Francisco city officials to take notice of the title. Speaking to NCB Bay Area, Mayor Daniel Lurie said, “There’s no accounting for taste or people’s terrible ideas. This is a bad one, and we reject it. It doesn’t speak for San Francisco values.”
In a statement to the San Francisco Chronicle, Supervisor Bilal Mahmood, who represents the Tenderloin, dubbed the game “deeply disturbing and unacceptable.”
“Turning violence against real people, including unhoused people, into entertainment is dehumanizing and should never be normalized,” he said. “I’m encouraged to see that the majority of San Franciscans recognize that this crosses a line and refuse to stand for it.”
While Biojout was previously boasting about the backlash on his social media accounts, he later removed the game from his online platform and issued a public apology over how his project depicted San Francisco’s citizens. He also revealed that he’d been inspired by an Alcatraz-themed Call of Duty map and said he often passes by the Tenderloin on his way to work.
“The game was not intended to provoke or to depict shooting real people. Its characters draw on a broad cross-section of San Francisco, across different backgrounds and walks of life, including people who work in tech. The familiar city details and Easter eggs are part of what makes it fun to play with friends,” he told the Chronicle.
Speaking to NBC Bay Area, Bijout said, “It was not intended to depict shooting real people or to target a particular demographic or group.”
Additionally, Biojout revealed that he refunded advertisers who promoted his game and removed all of his social media posts about it. He also donated the game’s total revenue to the Delancey Street Foundation, a nonprofit organization based in San Francisco that provides rehabilitation services and vocational training to convicted criminals and those suffering from substance abuse.
“I built and posted a zombie game set on San Francisco streets. The setting and the way I promoted it showed poor judgment. Targeting people struggling with addiction or homelessness was never my intention,” he wrote on Twitter/X.
The game was available on Biojout's NanoCorp AI website, a platform that runs online businesses using AI agents. It has since been removed, and the page is no longer available at the time of writing.

item.title: Zendaya will reportedly campaign in the Best Actress category for her role as "Chani" in Dune: Part III in the upcoming Oscars race.
item.description:
Zendaya will reportedly campaign in the Best Actress category for her role as Chani in Dune: Part III in the upcoming Oscars race.
“The move marks a shift from the first two films, where she was positioned in supporting actress,” said Variety. “The decision reflects Chani’s expanded role in the story.”
This larger, different role for Zendaya’s character in Dune: Part III has not gone unnoticed. IGN’s Jesse Schedeen recently wrote that “everything we’ve seen of Dune: Part Three so far suggests Chani is playing a vastly different role compared to the source material [Frank Herbert’s book Dune Messiah]. Her status quo is completely different. She isn’t Paul’s faithful concubine, pining for the day she can proudly bear his children. She’s rejected Paul and everything he stands for, preferring instead to live as a true Fremen, totally free and a servant to no one.”
It should be noted that none of the actors in either of the past two Dune movies have earned either an Oscar or a Golden Globe nomination for those films. Both Dune movies, however, were nominated in technical categories.
What Is Zendaya's Best Role?
